papers.title: Generating Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios from Role-Typed Signal Temporal Logic Specifications Drafted by Large Language Models
papers.comment: Manuscript submitted to IEEE OJ-ITS and is currently under review
papers.abstract: Safety-critical scenarios are rare in recorded driving and must be generated to test and train motion planners of automated vehicles. In guided diffusion models, each scenario type needs its own weighted objective, separate from the validity check. Optimized together with the attacker, the vehicle under test can cancel the attack or draw it toward itself. We state each scenario as a signal temporal logic specification with clauses typed by role. Every clause names the agent it may change and the agents it may read, and the vehicle under test reads the attacker only from the attack onset. A large language model drafts the specification from a description, and a type checker accepts it. A compiler derives the optimization: it edits a diffusion model's samples by the smallest change that satisfies the specification, each clause moves only its owner, the attacker is solved against the unreacted vehicle under test before its response, and the monitor of the same specification decides acceptance. On nuScenes and CommonRoad, judged independently of the specification, one parameter set produced valid scenarios at a rate 0.14 above a weighted objective tuned per scenario type, and descriptions yielded at least one valid scenario for 11 of the 16 pre-crash types expressible in the public data. Learned planners fail more often on the generated scenarios than on their seeds. Fine-tuning on them lowers a planner's failure rate on critical scenarios, and the time headway one clause of the label requires, not the generator, sets the size of the gain.
papers.title_zh: 由LLM起草的角色类型化信号时序逻辑规约生成安全关键驾驶场景
papers.summary_zh: 用LLM起草角色类型化STL规约，编译为优化问题，编辑扩散模型样本生成安全关键驾驶场景。

papers.title: CarlHOI: Counterfactual Predictive Imagination for Generalizable Multi-Humanoid Object Interaction under Constrained Environments
papers.abstract: Recent advances in physics-based humanoid control enable teams of varying sizes to coordinate their movements and cooperatively transport shared objects. However, adapting learned cooperative behaviors to unseen environmental constraints remains challenging, particularly when obstacles require coordinated detours and changes in team configuration. We propose CarlHOI, a counterfactual predictive imagination framework built upon a counterfactual-anchored relational latent world model (CarlWM) for human-object interaction (HOI), enabling multi-humanoid teams to adapt to unseen environmental constraints without retraining their underlying cooperative control policies. CarlHOI explicitly represents the shared object, individual humanoids, and environmental obstacles as interacting entities. Trained offline using counterfactual simulator rollouts, the model imagines alternative collective futures under different shared waypoint commands, predicting how the coupled humanoid team and object would respond. By evaluating these imagined outcomes through predicted progress, failure, and contact risks, and long-horizon value estimates, CarlHOI selects adaptive guidance commands while preserving the pretrained cooperative controller. We introduce a benchmark comprising three challenging obstacle-constrained transport tasks to evaluate adaptation and generalization. Despite being trained exclusively with four humanoids, our model generalizes without retraining to teams of two to ten humanoids, unseen obstacle geometries and placements, unseen objects, and novel combinations of environmental constraints. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved cooperative transport success over evaluated baselines across diverse configurations. Results highlight the potential of counterfactual predictive imagination to extend pretrained multi-humanoid cooperative skills beyond their original training conditions.
papers.title_zh: CarlHOI：面向受限环境下可泛化多人形机器人物体交互的反事实预测想象
papers.summary_zh: 用反事实关系隐空间世界模型，让多人形机器人团队无需重训即可适应未见的环境约束。

papers.title: Performance Evaluation of Nonlinear Model Predictive and Sliding Mode Controllers on a 4-Cable Spatial CSPR in Simscape
papers.comment: 7 pages, 13 figures, 2 tables. Prepared for the 13th RSI International Conference on Robotics and Mechatronics (ICRoM 2025), Tehran, Iran
papers.abstract: This paper offers a comprehensive comparative study between Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) applied to a spatial Cable-Suspended Parallel Robot (CSPR) actuated by four cables. The robot is modeled in two parallel ways: (i) via an analytical dynamic model with included cable elasticity and frictional losses, and (ii) in MATLAB Simscape Multibody, capturing realistic physical effects. Both controllers are implemented under identical reference trajectories, system constraints, and tuning strategies. Our results show that NMPC achieves superior tracking accuracy and stronger disturbance rejection compared to SMC, but at the cost of higher computational demand. Moreover, both controllers were tested on an analytical model of the robot and a Simscape model. The close agreement between the two, for both control schemes, confirms the accuracy of the analytical formulation and its consistency with the physics-based simulation. The study highlights the value of physics-based simulation as a complementary tool for validating advanced controllers under realistic conditions, and demonstrates that NMPC offers superior performance for the studied high-precision, constrained CSPR.
papers.title_zh: 四缆空间并联索驱动机器人在 Simscape 中的非线性模型预测与滑模控制性能评估
papers.summary_zh: 在 Simscape 中对比 NMPC 与滑模控制在四缆并联机器人上的跟踪精度和计算代价。

papers.title: Cache the Knowledge, Not Just the Prompt: Dynamic Datalog as the Action Language for LLM Agents
authors: Bruno Rucy Carneiro Alves de Lima
papers.abstract: An LLM agent that answers questions about a knowledge graph writes a program per question, and its tools evaluate each from scratch. We give the agent a Datalog REPL, a session over a dynamic Datalog engine, in which rules are inserted and retracted like facts while derived facts stay current. Prompt caching reuses the model's processing of what a session shares, and the Datalog REPL reuses the evaluation of it. On chains of questions over three knowledge graphs, agents reuse a relation that the REPL keeps in 179 of 180 cases, with two models, and write fewer output tokens: SQL and Python agents write 23 to 82% more. With SQL tables or a Python namespace, Claude Haiku 5.5 stores almost nothing for later questions, and a chain of seven questions at 13 million facts takes it a median of 48 and 56 s, against 31 s with the REPL. Claude Opus 5.5 matches the REPL by storing tables in SQL, and when the data changes it stores views, which are evaluated again at every read. A relation that the REPL keeps is read like a table and stays current like a view. Datalog is a niche language beside SQL and Python, and with thinking enabled the models answer as accurately with it.
papers.title_zh: 缓存知识而非仅缓存提示：以动态 Datalog 作为 LLM Agent 的动作语言
papers.summary_zh: 给 Agent 一个动态 Datalog REPL，复用知识图谱问答中已推导的关系，输出 token 比 SQL 和 Python 少。

papers.title: SparQ4D: Learning to Act through Sparse 4D Queries
papers.abstract: Successful manipulation requires a policy to understand where things are and how they will move, yet action demonstrations leave this spatiotemporal structure implicit. While explicit 4D supervision has proven effective, reducing the cost of dense 4D prediction remains challenging. This paper introduces SparQ4D, a lightweight yet expressive decoder that efficiently injects holistic 4D scene understanding into policies and improves success rates. At its core is a query-based decoder attached to a pretrained policy, which casts many spatialtemporal tasks into one unified interface (e.g. depth, 2D/3D point motion, multi-view correspondence, and hand-eye relations). This design enables efficient training and inference without sacrificing expressivity: the policy learns rich 4D structure from a small number of sampled queries during training, while the decoder can be removed at inference with zero additional overhead. Across multiple backbones, simulated environments, and real-world settings, SparQ4D achieves state-of-the-art manipulation performance, outperforming competing methods while training up to $5\times$ faster. Probing analyses further reveal that this 4D structure is recoverable from the policy.
papers.title_zh: SparQ4D：通过稀疏 4D 查询学习动作
papers.summary_zh: 在预训练策略上接一个基于查询的轻量解码器，以低开销注入 4D 场景理解并提升操作成功率。

papers.title: Grounded in Contact: Reducing Floating and Interpenetration Artifacts with Multimodal Skill-Effect Models
papers.comment: Under review. Project page: https://grounded-in-contact.github.io/. The second and third authors contributed equally
papers.abstract: Learning to predict the effects of contact-rich manipulation skills requires models that represent distinct outcome modes rather than a single expected result. Even for basic skills such as pushing, picking, and placing, small variations in contact conditions or object geometry can produce qualitatively different object motions under nearly identical states and actions. Deterministic and Gaussian models tend to average over these alternatives or represent them as a single broad distribution, obscuring distinct modes such as sliding, toppling, and rotating. We study probabilistic skill-effect models that learn multimodal distributions over object pose changes given partial point clouds and actions. We instantiate this abstraction with three representative model classes: mixture density networks, state tokenization, and flow matching, each paired with latent dynamics for next-step prediction. Across diverse objects and skills, explicitly multimodal models predict which outcome occurs more accurately than deterministic and Gaussian baselines. In planning, flow matching significantly improves task success over the deterministic baseline on every skill and achieves the highest success on every multi-step sequence. On a real robot, probabilistic models succeed at pick about twice as often as the deterministic baseline, providing evidence that probabilistic skill effects offer a practical abstraction for reasoning and planning under uncertainty.
papers.title_zh: 接触落地：用多模态技能效果模型减少漂浮与穿插伪影
papers.summary_zh: 用概率多模态模型预测推、抓、放等技能对物体位姿的影响，减少漂浮与穿插。

papers.title: Dr. Grasp-RL: Diverse and Robust Dexterous Grasping via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Human interaction with physical objects relies on a combination of dexterity and robustness. In robotic manipulation, dexterity requires not only flexible end effectors but also a diverse repertoire of manipulation strategies, while robustness requires closed-loop adaptation to disturbances and unexpected situations. Two prominent research directions in dexterous grasping have largely addressed these capabilities separately. Generative approaches model multimodal distributions to produce diverse grasp poses, but their reliance on open-loop execution can limit robustness. Reinforcement learning approaches learn closed-loop grasping policies, but can converge to a narrow range of successful grasping strategies, limiting behavioral diversity. We introduce a time-reversed curriculum with a coordinated reset mechanism that enables a simple MLP policy trained with PPO to capture multiple modes of the grasp-pose distribution while maintaining closed-loop control. Experiments demonstrate both diverse grasping behaviors and robust closed-loop execution. Trained on only approximately 400 objects, our policy further demonstrates strong generalization when evaluated on more than 20,000 unseen objects.
papers.title_zh: Dr. Grasp-RL：基于强化学习的多样且鲁棒的灵巧抓取
papers.summary_zh: 用强化学习同时获得灵巧抓取的多样性与闭环鲁棒性。

papers.title: Hashing Theorems Modulo Rewrites and Binder Permutation Enables Equivalence Search over 200k Mathlib Theorems
papers.abstract: Like all code, Lean libraries accumulate technical debt and structural deficiencies over the course of their development. A particular concern is duplicate theorems: different parts of a big library can unwittingly contain and prove the same theorem, duplicating maintenance efforts. Tools can help detect redundancy and clean up. For instance, Mathlib's duplicate-declarations linter compares theorem types syntactically after sorting top-level binders and erasing binder information and universe levels. If detecting an equivalence requires unfolding, reorientation, or logical transformations, it escapes this comparison. In this work, we present a method to detect theorems which are equivalent with regard to argument order and currying/uncurrying of dependent types. We implement our method for Lean. By applying it to Mathlib, a library of more than 200k theorems, we demonstrate that it is computationally cheap and scalable. We discuss how our work may enhance efforts to tackle the maintenance burden of Lean libraries.
papers.title_zh: 模重写与绑定变量置换的定理哈希，支持在 20 万条 Mathlib 定理上做等价搜索
papers.summary_zh: 用对重写和绑定变量置换不变的哈希，在 Mathlib 中检测重复的等价定理。

papers.title: Real-Time Kinodynamic Multi-Agent Motion Planning
papers.abstract: Coordinating large robot fleets, from warehouses to quadrotor swarms, requires collision-free trajectories that satisfy dynamic constraints and stay within speed and acceleration bounds. Existing kinodynamic multi-agent planners enforce these bounds during the search or through trajectory optimization after it, which limits fleet size and speed. We present Tickwise Actions to Kinodynamic Trajectories (TAKT), a framework that accounts for the dynamics before the search and reduces planning to a lattice search for double-integrator robots. TAKT analytically bounds the clearance lost when a discrete plan is smoothed and reserves this margin on the lattice. A closed-form convolution provably converts any valid plan into dynamically feasible trajectories with continuous-time collision avoidance. For robots spanning many lattice vertices, we introduce a diamond formulation that permits one-tick sideways yielding and adapt the Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) solvers PIBT and LaCAM to it. With 50 robots, our planners run over 2,000 times faster than the strongest baseline in 2D halls and over 100 times in 3D, with comparable or lower makespan and cost. They plan about a thousand robots in seconds in 2D, and tens of seconds in 3D, and replan up to a thousand robots in real time.
papers.title_zh: 实时动力学多智能体运动规划
papers.summary_zh: 把动力学约束提前到搜索之前，将多机器人规划化为双积分器的格点搜索，支持更大规模和更高速度。

papers.title: Feedback Completion Certificates for Repeated Dwell Tasks with Time Windows
papers.comment: 37 pages, including appendices with full proofs and experimental details
papers.abstract: An inspection robot may owe several measurements at the same station, each with a different window in which a dwell can begin. We ask what a feedback controller must retain about earlier visits to guarantee all remaining deadlines under bounded disturbances. For a common spatial predicate and dwell length, removing redundant windows orders the remaining obligations by both endpoints. On every history without an expired obligation, the served windows form a suffix. One boundary and one capped run length therefore preserve the future satisfaction of the original task. On a verified library of branching motion primitives we use this state to recover a feedback policy. For one task type a scalar threshold per run length suffices, with work linear in the number of listed branches per time layer for fixed dwell. Multiple types require a joint recursion. On a quadrotor inspection library the threshold sweep reduced the cost of constructing a reusable full-domain policy, while a sparse Boolean baseline answered a single initial query faster. In a two-station MuJoCo patrol, three task-aware filters all met every window in twelve paired runs each. Of eight initially certified runs, the completion filter retained the certificate in all eight, compared with three for safety-only filtering.
papers.title_zh: 带时间窗的重复驻留任务的反馈完成证书
papers.summary_zh: 刻画反馈控制器为保证有界扰动下的多个时间窗驻留任务需要保留的最小历史信息。

papers.title: Representation Alignment Is Only as Good as the Teacher's Behavioral Structure
papers.comment: 25 pages, 7 figures, 8 tables, including supplementary material
papers.abstract: Recent works align the intermediate features of vision-language-action (VLA) models with frozen vision encoders during fine-tuning, hoping to inject additional priors such as 3D awareness or affordances. Unlike in image generation, where teachers for representation alignment (REPA) are assessed with encoder-intrinsic metrics, teachers for VLAs are still chosen largely by heuristics. We show that this practice is unreliable: across 14 teachers and 16 manipulation tasks, under matched training budgets, no off-the-shelf vision encoder improves the clean success rate of $π_{0.5}$ by more than 1 point, and all of them reduce its success rate under perturbations by 10 to 39 points. Neither global semantics nor spatial structure, the criteria used in image generation, predicts which teachers help. We therefore propose the behavioral structure metric (BSM), which measures whether states that are close in a teacher's feature space are followed by similar expert actions within the same task. BSM correlates strongly with success rate under perturbations ($r=0.87$), and every off-the-shelf vision encoder scores below $π_{0.5}$ itself. Based on it, we introduce Behavior-Aware VLA Alignment (BAVA), a general VLA alignment protocol that favors vision encoders whose BSM exceeds the student's and stops alignment early according to the student's BSM during training. On SmolVLA, BAVA matches continuous alignment with one third of the alignment budget, and improves the average success rate by 4.6 points over unaligned fine-tuning. Our results suggest that representation alignment benefits VLAs only when the teacher encodes rich behaviorally relevant structure.
papers.title_zh: 表征对齐的效果取决于教师的行为结构
papers.summary_zh: 在 14 个教师和 16 个操作任务上发现，现成视觉编码器对齐不能提升 π0.5 的干净成功率，扰动下成功率还降低 10 到 39 个点。

papers.title: Self-Refining VLA Sampling
papers.comment: Accepted to the CoRL 2026 Learn@Deploy Workshop
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models typically use flow-based generative modeling to learn a rich, often multimodal, distribution of robot actions. Generating samples from flow-based methods involves iteratively updating random noise, and distinct noise samples from the same state can result in distinct trajectories and task outcomes. Existing test-time scaling methods improve action chunk generation via selection, aggregation, or correction, but commonly require the generation of large ensembles of candidates or the training of an external corrector. We adapt Predict-and-Perturb (P&P), a self-refinement procedure for flow-based models originally used for mode-seeking in video generation, to the robotics domain. We find that applying P&P to VLA models requires modifications to the refinement process used in video generation due to differences in the underlying structure of the data. Across 400 episodes of LIBERO evaluated using SmolVLA, P&P improves upon the stock baseline by 5.3 percentage points. Further, episode-level P\&P uncertainty correlates strongly with task failure (AUC 0.851).
papers.title_zh: VLA 自我精炼采样
papers.summary_zh: 把视频生成中的 Predict-and-Perturb 自精炼用于基于流的 VLA 动作采样，不需要大量候选或外部修正器。

papers.title: Specification-Aware Sparse Differentiation: Planning under Signal Temporal Logic with Sparsemax Robustness
papers.abstract: Gradient-based optimal control under a Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specification involves solving a nonlinear program whose constraints are smoothed robustness functions of the trajectory, and automatic differentiation without knowledge of sparsity computes the Jacobian and the Hessian that its solver needs in full. This often renders the problem computationally intractable. The dynamics and the specification prescribe a sparsity pattern through the STL syntax, the windows of the temporal operators and the variables that the predicates read. Standard tools such as CasADi recover this pattern by structural detection. In this work, we propose a method to prescribe such a pattern directly from the task specification. We show that our method allows us to exploit SparseMax, a recently proposed smooth robustness operator that is certifiably sparse and sound. Its derivative is exactly zero at every operand at or below a data-dependent threshold, which structural detection cannot see. We derive the patterns that expose this trajectory-dependent sparsity to sparse automatic differentiation, with a margin test for their reuse and Hessians confined to the variables of each constraint's support. We demonstrate the method on a dual-arm coordination task in which two arms share a hand-off zone divided into cells and one until constraint per scheduled visit keeps the other arm out of a cell until the visitor has left it. The two scenes are a zone of five cells and a circle of 64 cells, with single solves and closed-loop re-planning on a rigid-body simulation. Our exact-Hessian interior-point solves are up to 27 times faster than those with the sound log-sum-exp robustness in CasADi and IPOPT.
papers.title_zh: 规格感知的稀疏微分：基于 Sparsemax 鲁棒度的信号时序逻辑规划
papers.summary_zh: 直接由 STL 语法给出雅可比和海森矩阵的稀疏结构，降低 STL 约束最优控制的求解开销。

papers.title: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Recently, GPT-6 Astra demonstrates strong generalization in robot control, yet limited disclosure of its training leaves open how such capabilities can be reproduced. We introduce nanoAstra, an approach to training vision-language models (VLMs) for generalizable manipulation that combines semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning (CP-SFT). nanoAstra represents robot behavior as semantic steps composed of reusable, parameterized action primitives, guided by explicit progress descriptions. Meanwhile, CP-SFT uses an explicit robot-specific system prompt to constrain manipulation outputs to a structured action space, aiming to focus adaptation on robot-specific contexts and promote specialization while minimizing interference with broader pretrained capabilities. With this formulation, we train nanoAstra on more than 5,000 hours of robot data together with general VQA data. On RoboTwin 2.0's randomized benchmark, nanoAstra-9B achieves a 17.8% zero-shot success rate, substantially outperforming advanced VLA and WAM baselines as well as similarly sized VLMs. With inference faster than the corresponding motion execution on a single H20 GPU, our model supports action-chunk-like streaming execution that overlaps inference with motion, reducing the robot's idle time from 35.0% to 6.9%.
papers.title_zh: 训练 VLM 成为机器人操作基础模型的一瞥
papers.summary_zh: 提出 nanoAstra，用语义动作建模和保留能力的监督微调训练可泛化操作的 VLM。

papers.title: A2I-VLA: A Two-Stage Vision-Language-Action model with Semantic-Physical Alignment and Integration
papers.abstract: Force and tactile feedback provide essential information about physical interactions in contact-rich manipulation that visual observations alone cannot reliably capture.However, integrating these signals into vision-language-action (VLA) models remains challenging owing to the representational gap between visual-language semantics and physical measurements.To address this challenge, we propose A2I-VLA, a two-stage VLA framework that first learns semantically Aligned force-tactile representations and then Integrates them into a VLA model.In Stage I, a cross-modal alignment loss is introduced to promote correspondence between semantic and physical representations. The tactile and force feature streams are then integrated through a hierarchical multimodal fusion network, and the resulting representations are jointly supervised by future wrench and action prediction losses. The former encourages the model to anticipate physical responses, while the latter associates force-tactile observations with task-relevant manipulation behaviors.In Stage II, a gated cross-attention bridge module adaptively integrates the hierarchical physical features learned in Stage I into the VLA model to guide action generation.Real-world experiments demonstrate that the proposed A2I-VLA significantly outperforms the baseline PI05 across three contact-rich manipulation tasks, improving the success rate from 70% to 95%.
papers.title_zh: A2I-VLA：语义与物理对齐并融合的两阶段视觉语言动作模型
papers.summary_zh: 先对齐力觉和触觉表征与语义，再融入 VLA，用于接触密集型操作。

papers.title: Tacinf: A Unified Tactile Infrastructure for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Force-aware manipulation requires robots to infer appropriate interaction forces from task context and tactile feedback. We present Tacinf, a low-cost, modular infrastructure that enables policies to predict robot actions and fingertip forces from task language, vision, and touch. Task instructions can optionally specify the desired force level. Tacinf integrates simulation data synthesis and tactile benchmarking (Tabero), vision-tactile-language-action (VTLA) policy learning, handheld data collection using the same gripper as robot deployment (Tacumi), and task-aligned sim-to-real evaluation (Taco). Together, these components form an integrated workflow connecting data collection from multiple sources, foundation-model training, and hardware deployment. We validate each component, including the simulation data, benchmark, controller, and Tacumi, and are releasing the full stack as open source. A foundation model fine-tuned solely on tactile simulation data transfers zero-shot to different real-robot tasks. Across eight policy variants, mean task success rates are strongly correlated between simulation and the real robot (Pearson r=0.998, mean maximum rank violation MMRV=0.010). For the four policies with reported force measurements, mean grip force is higher under firm instructions than under gentle instructions on all three tasks in both domains. When both object positions and instances are randomized, a mixture of teleoperation, simulation, and Tacumi data raises mean real-robot task success from 20% with teleoperation alone to 60%.
papers.title_zh: Tacinf：面向机器人操作的统一触觉基础设施
papers.summary_zh: 提供低成本模块化的触觉数据合成、基准、VTLA 策略学习、手持采集和仿真到真机评测的完整流程。

papers.title: InfoField3D: Differentiable Information Field for Embodied Task-Oriented View Planning
papers.abstract: Effective task execution requires embodied agents to select observation positions that provide sufficient task-relevant information. Existing approaches typically predict viewpoints with learned models or score discrete candidates, but they either struggle to incorporate new constraints such as reachability or require extensive candidate evaluation to search. We introduce InfoField3D, which lifts geometry-bound information into a differentiable analytic field, whose value at each 3D observation position represents the task-required information accessible there. It uses low-order spherical harmonics to encode directional information responses and analytic line integrals of Gaussian occupancy functions to model occlusion along lines of sight. This formulation casts task-driven camera placement as a well-studied constrained continuous optimization problem, enabling both flexible incorporation of constraints through the feasible domain and efficient viewpoint search even in the presence of occlusion. Experiments show that InfoField3D compactly preserves the pointwise information landscape with high fidelity and generally recommends higher-quality, more robust viewpoints at lower search cost than the evaluated baselines. Controlled evaluations with a frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policy further suggest that the recommended views can improve downstream task performance under information-limited initial viewpoints.
papers.title_zh: InfoField3D：面向具身任务的可微信息场视角规划
papers.summary_zh: 把几何信息提升为可微解析信息场，在三维空间中直接优化任务相关的观察位置。

papers.title: Force2Act: A Force-Aware Visuomotor Policy for Generalizable Compliant Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Contact-rich manipulation requires a robot to regulate the force it applies, not only where it moves. Existing force-aware policies learn this force from demonstrations and therefore reproduce the force levels they were trained on, which fails once the interaction demands more force than any demonstration. We present Force2Act, a hybrid force-position policy built on two complementary mechanisms. A global force policy plans the motion and the interaction force once per action chunk, with force represented relative to the measured interaction, so that the planned force scales with the load. Between planning steps, a reactive compliance policy, termed Mixture of Force Experts, identifies at every control step the force expert that governs the interaction and regulates the force through it, so that the contact holds when it changes within a chunk. We further introduce Force2Act-Bench, a simulation benchmark of five contact-rich tasks that gives the community a common and repeatable way to test force-aware policies and measure how well they regulate the interaction force. Force2Act achieves an overall success rate of 93.8%, compared with 77.0% for the strongest baseline, and its reactive regulation reduces the failures on block pivoting from 30 to 10 of 150 trials. On a real robot, Force2Act reaches an average success rate of 94.2% over four tasks, against at most 27.5% for the baselines.
papers.title_zh: Force2Act：面向可泛化柔顺机器人操作的力感知视觉运动策略
papers.summary_zh: 混合力位策略按负载缩放规划力，并用混合力专家做反应式柔顺，超出演示力水平时仍能操作。

papers.title: FunGrasp-Zero: Field-Conditioned Graph Attention Policy for Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Functional Grasping
papers.abstract: Dexterous functional grasping is critical for robotic tool use, yet current dexterous hands exhibit substantial morphological diversity. This hardware heterogeneity makes cross-embodiment functional grasping a fundamental but largely unexplored problem. Existing functional grasping methods use retargeted hand poses as guidance, tying task representation to a specific embodiment and failing to explicitly capture object-centric functional contact intent, limiting generalization across hands. To address this, we propose FunGrasp-Zero, a reinforcement learning framework for zero-shot cross-embodiment functional grasping. Instead of relying on embodiment-specific joint configuration, FunGrasp-Zero captures functional intent via an object-centric, cross-embodiment-consistent contact map, adapted to heterogeneous hands through morphological mapping. We construct a hand-object potential field from mapped contact regions, yielding attractive and repulsive guidance vectors. A Field-Conditioned Graph Attention Network (FC-GAT) leverages these vectors to coordinate multi-finger motion across hands, while a potential field reward guides fingers toward target regions and penalizes non-target collisions to enforce functional alignment and stability. We further establish X-FunBench for cross-embodiment functional grasping, evaluating both physical grasp success and functional intent preservation across hands. Evaluated on X-FunBench, our unified policy, co-trained on four embodiments, achieves 86% average grasp success rate across five unseen hands on novel objects. Deployed on four unseen physical hands (Leap, Inspire, Sharpa, Wuji) for novel object grasping, the policy achieves 80% average success rate without fine-tuning. To our knowledge, FunGrasp-Zero is the first RL-based framework to achieve zero-shot cross-embodiment functional grasping across unseen hands in both simulation and the real world.
papers.title_zh: FunGrasp-Zero：用场条件图注意力策略实现零样本跨本体灵巧功能抓取
papers.summary_zh: 以物体中心的功能接触意图取代特定灵巧手的关节配置，用强化学习实现零样本跨手抓取。

papers.title: Implementation and Software-in-the-Loop Evaluation of a Trans-Domain Digital Twin Architecture for Autonomous Guidance of the Phoenix VTOL UAV Without Online GNSS
papers.comment: 34 pages, 17 figures, 4 tables. Software-in-the-loop evaluation of GNSS-independent Phoenix VTOL guidance using a trans-domain digital twin architecture. Source code and reproducibility materials: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24419538
papers.abstract: Autonomous UAV guidance in emergency response, infrastructure monitoring, and cargo transportation requires reliable navigation. However, satellite-based positioning may become unavailable or unreliable in enclosed spaces, blind spots caused by natural obstacles and structures, and environments affected by radio interference and signal spoofing during electronic warfare. This study designs, implements, and evaluates a system based on a Trans-Domain Digital Twin (TDDT) for autonomous guidance of the Phoenix VTOL UAV. Independent navigation, flight dynamics, and meteorological models are coordinated within a cycle of state estimation, prediction, decision-making, command execution, and feedback. Data from inertial, magnetic, pressure, and airspeed sensors, together with environmental information, form the basis for estimation and prediction. Furthermore, a shared state, temporal synchronization, preservation of information provenance, and command traceability establish continuity between models and decisions. The system was tested with a simulated physical twin in a software-in-the-loop environment. Vertical takeoff, movement toward the destination, landing, and autonomous stopping were recorded, and the dynamic model was adjusted to a limited extent based on sensor-derived feedback. Separating the evaluation reference from navigation inputs enabled independent assessment of positioning error and computational performance. The results confirm operational coordination, decision traceability, and closed-loop guidance under the tested conditions, providing a reproducible platform for the development and evaluation of navigation without satellite-based positioning.
papers.title_zh: 无在线 GNSS 的 Phoenix 垂直起降无人机跨域数字孪生自主制导的实现与软件在环评估
papers.summary_zh: 设计并在软件在环中评估基于跨域数字孪生、不依赖在线 GNSS 的无人机自主制导系统。

papers.title: Your Diffusion-Based Driving Planner Only Needs a Nudge
papers.comment: Autonomous driving, Trajectory Planning, Diffusion-based Planners, Reinforcement Learning, RL Post-training, Off-policy RL
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based planners capture the multimodality of human driving behavior well, yet covariate shift in closed-loop driving can lead them to generate trajectories that result in collisions or road departures. Reinforcement learning (RL) finetuning offers a promising way to tackle this issue, but applying it to diffusion-based planners is complicated by their iterative denoising process and receding-horizon execution. We find that small adjustments to the planned trajectories can prevent many of these unsafe outcomes. Motivated by this observation, we propose PlanNudge, which preserves the learned planning capabilities of a pretrained diffusion-based planner by freezing it and trains a lightweight policy that we call the nudge policy. At each planning step, the nudge policy outputs a nudge, a two-dimensional adjustment of the speed and curvature of the plan from the frozen planner. The nudge policy is a multilayer perceptron that predicts the nudge in a single forward pass, and both dimensions directly change the motion of the vehicle, so standard off-policy RL can train it in closed-loop simulation. We evaluate PlanNudge on nuPlan, a large-scale autonomous driving benchmark based on real-world driving data. In all six settings, PlanNudge matches or exceeds the final scores of the previous state-of-the-art RL finetuning method while using about one sixth as many environment steps and less than one fifth as much model compute. We also provide guidelines for reward shaping, value learning, and exploration when using off-policy RL to post-train autonomous driving planners. Our results are reported with means and standard deviations over six training runs. Project page: https://zerlinwang.github.io/plannudge/
papers.title_zh: 你的扩散式驾驶规划器只需要轻轻一推
papers.summary_zh: 冻结预训练扩散规划器，只训练轻量模块对轨迹做小幅修正，以减少闭环驾驶中的碰撞和驶出道路。

papers.title: One Million Tokens in 20GB: Calibration-Free 2-Bit SRFT KV-Cache Compression for Looped MoE Inference on Apple Silicon
papers.abstract: Long-context inference on unified-memory edge machines is governed by KV-cache capacity and memory bandwidth. On a 32 GB Apple M6 Mac mini (26.8 GB Metal working set, 150 GB/s DRAM), the 26.4B looped Mixture-of-Experts model Inkling-2-Mini (48 logical visits, 1M native context) exhausts memory by 64K tokens in stock oMLX (and by 512K even after fixing its 40 sliding-window visits to bounded ring buffers). We show that three structural properties of modern hybrid NoPE architectures -- bounded sliding windows, a 1,024-token banded relative bias whose tail is identically zero, and unit-RMS value normalization -- combine with an orthonormal Subsampled Randomized Fourier Transform (SRFT) to enable calibration-free, scale-free 2.000-bit Value and 2.125-bit Key Lloyd-Max compression (2.0625 effective bits/coordinate, $7.76\times$ smaller than bf16) on the 8 global visits' far prefix $[0, N-1024)$, merged with the exact bf16 local window and learned sink via online log-sum-exp. A custom GQA-packed Metal decode kernel with a 256-entry half4 LUT and Block-8 lazy exp2 rescaling reaches 73.4 GB/s and runs Inkling-2-Mini at 17.09 tok/s at 256K ($3.36\times$ faster than bf16), 13.81 tok/s at 512K, and 9.52 tok/s at 1,048,576 tokens in 19.49 GiB peak memory (4.37 GiB KV). Across $4\times 4096$ WikiText-2 windows, 3.06-bit SRFT is lossless ($Δ$PPL $= -0.007$), 2.56-bit K3/V2 adds $+0.024$, and 2.06-bit adds $+0.130$ while achieving 100% (3/3) exact 7-digit passkey retrieval at 8K, 16K, and 32K.
papers.title_zh: 20GB 装下一百万 token：面向 Apple Silicon 上循环 MoE 推理的免校准 2 比特 SRFT KV Cache 压缩
papers.summary_zh: 用 SRFT 把 KV Cache 压到 2 比特，使 26.4B 循环 MoE 模型在 32GB 的 Mac mini 上跑 1M 上下文。

papers.title: ViewPACT: Multi-View Geometric Augmentation and Pose-Action Co-Training for Viewpoint-Robust Manipulation
papers.abstract: Image policies are scalable but remain brittle to camera viewpoint changes. On LIBERO, we identify proprioception as an input shortcut: masking robot states sharply degrades several policies, while retraining from images alone recovers much of the loss. We introduce ViewPACT, an image policy trained with privileged geometric supervision. Auxiliary objectives recover end-effector and task-relevant object poses in the camera frame, while deployment requires only RGB observations. Joint geometric supervision improves mean simulation success from 37.4% to 78.4% under unseen external-camera viewpoints, with more modest gains under separately evaluated object, scene, and camera-intrinsic shifts. Across four real-robot tasks, combining simulated and real-image geometric supervision achieves 68.1% mean success, versus 3.1% for fixed-view behavior cloning and 30.6% for the strongest evaluated alternative. These results support geometric supervision for viewpoint robustness in the evaluated fixed-view demonstration setting.
papers.title_zh: ViewPACT：面向视角鲁棒操作的多视角几何增强与位姿动作联合训练
papers.summary_zh: 用特权几何监督训练图像策略，未见外部相机视角下仿真平均成功率从 37.4% 提升到 78.4%。

papers.title: HiPerfCC-StateReuse: Ciphertext Reuse for Fast Confidential GPU Data Movement
papers.abstract: Confidential GPUs offer near-native on-device compute performance, but transfers between CPU and GPU TEEs through untrusted host memory require bulk CPU encryption and decryption, even for unchanged data. Existing software techniques overlap or parallelize these operations but retain their per-byte CPU cost. Reusing exported ciphertext could avoid this work, but GPU TEE firmware enforces direction-specific encryption keys and fresh per-transfer initialization vectors (IVs), preventing direct reuse. We introduce ciphertext rebinding, a purely software primitive enabling repeated and cross-GPU ciphertext reuse on existing GPU TEEs without hardware changes, while preserving confidentiality, integrity, and freshness. Specifically, ciphertext rebinding exploits the separation between ciphertext-dependent and IV-dependent components in GPU TEE's AES-GCM authentication: a GPU-precomputed summary under the destination key can enable the CPU to update authentication tags without processing the payload. With this modification, GPU's subsequent read on the retained ciphertext can still proceed through the GPU's hardware-fixed copy-engine interfaces, which cannot be modified by software. An additional GPU correction step can then compensate for differences in the keys and IVs to recover the original plaintext. By retaining GPU-exported ciphertext in untrusted host memory, ciphertext rebinding avoids bulk CPU decryption and re-encryption, improving effective bandwidth for GPU-state restoration and sharing. We implement this primitive in HiPerfCC-StateReuse through only driver and library changes, combining batched submissions with pipelined GPU processing and copy-engine transfers. We evaluate transfer efficiency and CPU overhead through microbenchmarks, and application performance through three case studies: model switching, key-value cache offloading, and cross-instance cache sharing.
papers.title_zh: HiPerfCC-StateReuse：面向机密 GPU 高速数据搬运的密文复用
papers.summary_zh: 提出纯软件的密文重绑定，让现有 GPU TEE 重复复用已导出的密文，省去 CPU 加解密开销。

papers.title: BO-COMM: Bidirectional Optical System for Simultaneous Localization and Communication in Swarm Robotics
papers.abstract: Swarm robotics experiments need to track where robots are, know what state each robot is in, and feed environmental information back to them. Reporting states over a shared radio channel can suffer from contention as the number of robots grows, while static fiducial markers provide pose but cannot report changing states. We present BO-COMM, a bidirectional optical system that observes pose and state through one camera and returns environmental cues through light. Each Colias IV robot, fitted with a CEU-PLUS extension unit, carries a ring of 12 LEDs: a five-bit marker encodes heading, and the remaining seven bits display one of 52 state codes. An overhead camera locates robot centers by ring-based voting and decodes position, heading and state for all visible robots from a single frame. In the downstream direction, a projector renders spatial cues such as virtual pheromone fields, and an infrared channel delivers addressed commands. At 2048x1280 resolution, image-processing time increases only modestly from 2 to 30 robots. Path-following, color-reporting and multi-pheromone experiments show the system closing the loop between optical state reports and projected environmental feedback in a 2.50 x 1.56 m arena.
papers.title_zh: BO-COMM：面向集群机器人同时定位与通信的双向光学系统
papers.summary_zh: 用一台相机读取机器人 LED 环中的位姿与状态编码，并用光向机器人回传环境信息。

papers.title: Distributed Interactive Conformal Prediction for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems increasingly rely on learning-enabled components and distributed algorithms for perception, estimation, and control, introducing uncertainty that makes it challenging to satisfy mission requirements. Conformal prediction quantifies uncertainty with distribution-free guarantees, but existing methods do not address the challenging combination of dependence among robots, distributed calibration, and the distribution shift induced when calibrated uncertainty bounds modify the closed-loop system. We introduce Multi-Agent Interactive Conformal Prediction (MA-ICP), a distributed framework for computing robustness margins in heterogeneous systems to satisfy mission requirements with high probability. MA-ICP aggregates robot-level nonconformity scores, which measure errors in modeled or estimated quantities, into one mission-level score per robot class, allowing dependence among robots within each mission. Mission-level scores and quantiles are computed using neighbor-to-neighbor communication in a finite number of communication rounds. Updating the robustness margins changes robot trajectories and distributed algorithm outputs, so we use class-dependent score sensitivities to upper bound the shift in mission-level scores. We then establish calibration-conditional coverage guarantees per robot class for the updated margins. We demonstrate MA-ICP on cooperative payload control, formation control with obstacle avoidance, and distributed target tracking missions.
papers.title_zh: 多智能体系统的分布式交互式保形预测
papers.summary_zh: 提出 MA-ICP，在机器人间存在依赖和分布偏移时分布式计算满足任务要求的鲁棒裕度。

papers.title: graspit-py: A Python Interface to GraspIt! for Grasp Planning Under Pose and Friction Uncertainty
papers.comment: Technical report. 31 pages, 8 figures, 9 tables. Code: https://github.com/coenwerem/graspit-py
papers.abstract: In simulated multifingered grasps, pose error can change contacts formed during hand closure, while friction uncertainty changes the loads supported by those contacts. Existing C++ APIs and ROS 1 services provide programmatic GraspIt! access but require native bindings or a service transport layer for Python use and application-specific integration of contact geometry with uncertainty sampling. A Python workflow for these studies must connect native closure and contacts to caller-defined wrench scores, uncertainty samples, and command reconstruction. We present graspit-py, a Python interface to native GraspIt! operations that supplies this workflow. The interface provides native scene access, contact-wrench analysis, and configurable approach planning under pose and friction uncertainty. A grasp record associates the object-relative palm pose and closed independent coordinates with nominal contacts and quality scores evaluated under sampled pose and friction conditions. Our MuJoCo exporter derives serial hinge chains and affine joint couplings, including nonzero reference angles, and preserves individual collision components. Across 75 configurations of five hand models, maximum discrepancy between source and exported palm-frame vertex sets was approximately 1.3 micrometers against a 100-micrometer geometry tolerance. We isolated reference-angle and collision-component effects through controlled ablations and validated 1,920 directional task-wrench capacity calculations against independent Cartesian-force linear programs. In a common GraspIt! workload, median reset-close-score-state cycle latency through direct Python was 10.7% lower than through persistent ROS 1 services. An executable export-plan-reconstruct workflow and grasp examples on six hand models demonstrate how the contact, score, and joint representations support numerical analysis and command reconstruction.
papers.title_zh: graspit-py：位姿与摩擦不确定性下抓取规划的 GraspIt! Python 接口
papers.summary_zh: 提供 GraspIt! 的 Python 接口，支持在位姿与摩擦不确定性下做多指抓取研究。

papers.title: DMPT-Swarm: A Directional Mass-Preserving Transform for Decentralized Swarm Navigation in Obstacle Environments
papers.comment: Accepted by the Conference on Decision and Control (CDC) 2026
papers.abstract: This paper presents a decentralized microscopic control framework for swarm navigation in obstacle environments, given a precomputed macroscopic trajectory represented by Gaussian mixture models (GMMs). To generate obstacle-aware reference locations without inter-agent communication, we first employ affine transport between multivariate normal (MVN) distributions under the Wasserstein-2 metric. We then propose a directional mass-preserving transform (DMPT) to incorporate obstacle effects by modifying radial transport while preserving directional structure. Based on the transformed references, a local artificial potential field (APF)-based controller is applied for navigation. Each agent operates independently, reducing communication and computational burden. Simulation results demonstrate improved efficiency and obstacle avoidance compared to conventional APF-based methods

papers.title: T-Tac: A Soft and Thin Active Thermal Tactile Sensor for Robotic In-Grasp Material Identification
papers.abstract: Accurate material identification is important for robotic manipulation, yet vision-based methods face challenges when materials have similar appearances. Herein, we report T-Tac, a soft, thin, active thermal tactile sensor that identifies materials through their transient thermal responses. T-Tac integrates a polyimide film heater with an ionic conductive film temperature sensor, providing controlled thermal excitation and resistance-based temperature measurement in a film assembly suitable for mounting on robotic grippers. Single-sided transient plane source modeling and finite element simulations relate the thermal response to material thermal properties, while calibration and repeated measurements characterize the heating and sensing performance. Loading experiments at room and elevated temperatures further characterize the sensor response under an applied force. A hybrid classification framework concatenates extracted thermal descriptors with multiscale convolutional neural network features and uses an ExtraTrees classifier for material prediction. Experiments on 12 materials achieve a mean classification accuracy of 92.69\% using a 3 s heating pulse and a 10 s observation window. These results support T-Tac as a compact approach to integrating active thermal material sensing into robotic end effectors. This work shed a light on the new approach for robotic material identification.

papers.title: An End-to-End Theory for Compositional Symbolic Execution: From Expressive Specifications to SMT (Extended Version)
papers.abstract: Compositional symbolic execution (CSE) is a powerful technique for program verification and bug-finding, yet existing formal theories of CSE do not sufficiently bridge the gap between idealised models and real-world tools. We present progress towards a foundational, realistic, end-to-end theory of CSE in the Rocq proof assistant. Our theory advances realism at both ends of the CSE pipeline: it supports an expressive frontend with algebraic data types, logical functions, and lemmas; it also provides a verified connection to SMT-LIB compliant SMT solvers. Our contributions include: (1) a CSE theory that captures practical verification patterns; (2) a standalone, reusable Rocq mechanisation of the SMT-LIB standard; (3) a proven-correct encoding from CSE backend queries to SMT-LIB queries that accounts for semantic discrepancies and optimises using type information; and (4) empirical evidence for the backend by extracting our verified SMT-LIB encoding and running it alongside the CSE tool Gillian's own encoding on a majority of its solver queries.

papers.title: Refined, Reliable and Reproducible: Algorithmic Analysis and Reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder
papers.abstract: Cosmic voids are vast underdense regions of the Universe that encode valuable information about its large-scale structure and evolution. By extending spherical voids into overlapping sphere structures, the Popcorn Void Finder demonstrated an improved statistical characterization of cosmic void populations. However, its origin as a research prototype progressively hindered its maintainability and extensibility. Moreover, post-publication algorithmic modifications have not been systematically evaluated, leaving their statistical and computational consequences insufficiently characterized. In this work, we present a comprehensive reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder, prioritizing algorithmic transparency, maintainability, and reproducibility. We document the complete identification procedure, revisit the original algorithmic choices, and evaluate their statistical and computational consequences. Comparisons between implementations revealed a significant change in the behavior of the Void Size Function, which is now characterized by a power-law regime transitioning to a Schechter-like distribution. These changes not only provide a better characterization of void sizes, but enable a new and more robust method to the determination of the shot-noise dominated regime, without implicit dependencies on internal finder parameters present in previous works. Performance benchmarks demonstrate a 1.62x speedup in spherical void identification and a substantial improvement in overlap-removal throughput. We determined the Popcorn algorithm to be negatively affected by load imbalance, and found a speedup of 63x in a tested configuration with a newly introduced early growth termination criterion. These results establish a more maintainable and reproducible foundation for popcorn void identification, while clarifying the statistical and computational trade-offs that govern its performance.
papers.title_zh: 精炼、可靠、可复现：Popcorn 空洞查找器的算法分析与重新实现
papers.summary_zh: 对宇宙空洞查找器 Popcorn 做算法分析并重新实现，评估后续算法修改的统计和计算影响。

papers.title: LIBERO-MOR: A Multimodal Robustness Benchmark Across the Vision-Language-Action Pipeline
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have achieved strong performance on robot manipulation benchmarks. Translating this progress into reliable deployment calls for systematic evaluation of how policies respond to variations throughout the robot interaction loop. We introduce LIBERO-MOR, a multimodal robustness benchmark across the vision-language-action pipeline. Built on standard LIBERO, it covers five deployment-facing domains: vision, language, proprioception, action execution, and environment. The benchmark comprises 22 deployment-inspired perturbations, each evaluated at three severity levels across 40 tasks under a paired clean-perturbed protocol, enabling controlled and reproducible comparisons. We evaluate seven representative VLA models spanning diverse action-generation mechanisms. Our experiments reveal substantial robustness gaps behind high clean-task success, together with shared vulnerabilities and distinct model-specific failure patterns across domains. Severity analysis further distinguishes progressive degradation, collapse at stronger interventions, and failures triggered at the mildest tested level. By connecting aggregate performance to pipeline domains, individual perturbations, and intervention strength, LIBERO-MOR provides a systematic framework for diagnosing VLA robustness and guiding the development of more reliable robot policies.

papers.title: DeRail: Escaping Trajectory Priors via Counterfactual Action Steering for Mid-Execution Instruction Switching
papers.abstract: Robots operating in the real world must often adapt when user instructions change mid-execution, yet current instruction-conditioned robot policies, including Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and World-Action Models (WAMs), are largely evaluated under fixed-instruction episodes. We study mid-execution instruction switching and identify trajectory hijacking as a key failure mode, where the policy fails to redirect sufficiently toward the switched target, with its post-switch behavior remaining fully or partially drawn toward trajectories associated with non-target tasks. We propose Counterfactual Action Steering (CAS), a training-free, model-agnostic inference-time method that identifies interfering non-target tasks, queries the same policy with corresponding counterfactual instructions, and uses target--counterfactual action differences to steer execution away from interfering trajectory priors. Experiments on LIBERO-Goal-Switch and CALVIN-Custom-Switch across five VLA and WAM policies, together with real-robot evaluation, show that CAS consistently improves switching success; for example, on CALVIN-Custom-Switch in the $[15,21]$ switching range, CAS improves $π_{0.5}$ from 5.8\% to 54.6\%. Successful CAS-guided rollouts further provide higher-quality self-training supervision than vanilla successful rollouts with the same number of trajectories, yielding stronger policies that generalize to unseen later instruction switches. Code will be made publicly available.

papers.title: VTLA-RL: Learning Visuotactile Policies for Load-Adaptive Grasping
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action foundation models learn general manipulation priors, but object mass and local slip are difficult to infer from vision alone. Changing loads require contact-driven grasp adjustments that demonstrations collected under fixed conditions may not adequately cover. We present VTLA-RL to study visuotactile grasping policies and their reinforcement learning (RL) post-training under varying loads. Our main approach shares a visual encoder between tactile-image histories and RGB inputs to jointly generate and execute motion and bilateral force targets in a unified action space. Mixed real and simulated demonstrations first establish motion and contact priors. Two-stage multi-task RL then uses only simulated interaction to optimize the policy through task-success returns without continued real-demonstration supervision, and the trained policy deploys directly to real robots. We compare tactile representations and RL post-training routes in simulation and separately evaluate load variation and placement perturbations on hardware. The full method achieves higher grasping success than the supervised initialization, while RL post-training gains differ across approaches, providing empirical evidence for choosing representations and training approaches for this task.

papers.title: Data-Driven Trajectory Prediction via Probabilistic Modes and Constrained Optimization
papers.abstract: Predicting the future trajectories of surrounding agents is a fundamental requirement for safe autonomous driving. Since agent intent is inherently uncertain, multimodal prediction is essential to account for the full range of plausible future behaviors. We introduce Probabilistic Modes and Constrained Optimization trajectory prediction (ProMo-CoOp), a two-stage data-driven framework. At design time, trajectories are clustered into behavioral modes and a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) provides probabilistic mode assignments. At prediction time, a candidate trajectory is generated for each mode by solving a convex optimization problem that enforces consistency with the observed trajectory and uses the precomputed mode assignments to guide prediction toward the selected behavioral mode. The framework also supports Signal Temporal Logic (STL)-derived behavioral constraints, with predicate satisfaction probabilities estimated using Conditional Flow Matching (CFM). Experiments show that ProMo-CoOp outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, and that STL-based constraints can further improve performance when the predicted predicate satisfactions are reliable.

papers.title: IRIS: Inverse Dynamics from Random Exploration with Eye-in-hand Sensing
papers.abstract: Imagine-then-execute methods offer a promising paradigm for video-based manipulation, where a video planner predicts future visual subgoals and an inverse dynamics model (IDM) grounds them into robot actions. Despite their promise, these methods remain limited by action grounding. First, the IDM is typically trained on limited task-specific demonstrations and can generalize poorly even when given oracle visual subgoals, indicating that action grounding remains a bottleneck beyond visual planning errors. Second, precise execution benefits from eye-in-hand observations, but eye-in-hand video planning is both hard to learn and hard to scale: the viewpoint moves with the robot, and such videos are scarce at internet scale. To overcome these challenges, we propose IRIS, a video-based manipulation framework that learns a highly generalizable, execution-aware IDM. First, IRIS scales action grounding by pretraining the IDM on task-agnostic random exploration data, which provides diverse visual state transitions paired with robot actions without human task annotation. Second, it extends the IDM with eye-in-hand sensing through a two-stage training scheme, without requiring eye-in-hand video planning. Extensive simulation and real-world experiments show that IRIS improves action grounding and data efficiency, enables more precise execution, and achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art manipulation policies.
papers.title_zh: IRIS：基于手眼感知随机探索的逆动力学
papers.summary_zh: 用随机探索数据训练手眼视角的逆动力学模型，解决视频规划后动作落地的瓶颈。

papers.title: Distilling Touch into Vision-Only Policies for Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.abstract: Tactile feedback benefits contact-rich manipulation, yet deploying tactile sensors introduces additional hardware and maintenance requirements. Tactile experience can still provide effective supervision for policies that operate without tactile sensors at deployment. Tactile imagination methods such as TacImag remove this hardware dependency by predicting tactile observations, but retain a reconstruction stage whose errors can propagate into action generation. We present TacitTouch, a distillation framework that transfers tactile-guided behavior directly into a vision-only policy. The core shift is from "learn to imagine what touch would feel like" to "learn to behave as if you could feel touch": the student directly learns tactile-guided action patterns without reconstructing tactile observations. A frozen visuotactile teacher supervises the student's denoising predictions and intermediate action representations at the same noisy action and flow time. Training also uses demonstrated-action supervision. Deployment retains only the visual policy, with no tactile encoder, expert, or generator. Across four simulated UniVTAC tasks and four real-world tasks, TacitTouch achieves absolute improvements of 16.0% and 22.5% in mean success rate over vision-only control, respectively. The absolute gaps to the teacher using measured tactile input are only 2.0% and 3.75%, respectively. In robustness tests, it also outperforms TacImag, with absolute gains of up to 20.0% in mean success rate. Project page: https://pier-lab.github.io/tacittouch/

papers.title: Doing More with Less: Complex Manipulation with a Contact-Adaptive Robotic Hand
papers.abstract: Anthropomorphic robotic hands offer the potential to manipulate objects designed for human hands in environments adapted to human use. However, developing a robotic hand that replicates the human hand in terms of morphology, degrees of freedom, force output, durability, and sensing capabilities remains a formidable challenge, as these requirements inherently involve trade-offs. Here, we propose a robotic hand mechanism designed to address several of these trade-offs by enabling contact-adaptive finger motion, slender fingers, a wide grasping range, and sustained gripping force. We also introduce a motion glove based on quaternion swing-twist decomposition to extract human manipulation intentions and translate them into robotic hand commands, along with a forearm-mounted interface designed to enhance the operator's sense of embodiment. Experimental demonstrations show that a robotic hand with limited active degrees of freedom and no tactile sensing can perform complex tasks, including smartphone pickup and charging, in-hand manipulation, object unboxing and repackaging, and cutting and tying cords, through the combination of the proposed mechanism and effective bimanual coordination.
papers.title_zh: 事半功倍：用接触自适应机械手完成复杂操作
papers.summary_zh: 提出手指细长、抓取范围大的接触自适应机械手机构，并配套四元数动捕手套提取人类操作意图。

papers.title: VAPY: Circuit Optimization with Backpropagation
papers.abstract: Parameter sensitivities of analog circuits enable the use of gradient-based design optimization methods and unlock a range of sensitivity analyses. However, it remains a challenge to compute exact design parameter sensitivities for circuits that use PDKs, which use Verilog-A device models comprised of thousands of lines of code. Finite difference methods, which estimate gradients through simulation, require N + 1 to 2N simulations for each gradient depending on the method, which can become prohibitively expensive when many parameters are optimized. We present VAPY, a Verilog-A to JAX transpiler that compiles Verilog-A device models into autodifferentiable JAX code, enabling optimization with Circulax, a JAX-based circuit simulator. VAPY employs taint analysis to ensure only the necessary control-flow is rewritten with JAX-compatible calls, reducing control-flow overheads. We use VAPY and Circulax to optimize three analog circuits implemented in the SkyWater SKY130 PDK, which is built on the BSIM4 device model. VAPY-generated model gradients closely match finite-difference gradients, achieving comparable design quality in over 40X fewer circuit solves and up to 40% lower loss than Bayesian optimization.
papers.title_zh: VAPY：基于反向传播的电路优化

papers.title: PhysPPF: Learning Robotic Manipulation with Past, Present, and Future Physical Representations
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have advanced robotic manipulation, yet complex tasks requiring both precise 3D contact and long-horizon coordination remain challenging. Most existing studies enhance spatial perception or temporal reasoning in VLAs separately. Spatial methods primarily inject geometric or affordance priors into current-frame perception without tracking multi-step transitions, while history-aware and world-model VLAs typically capture past context or future dynamics in 2D feature or pixel spaces, either lacking explicit 3D contact cues or incurring high generation overhead. To address this, we propose PhysPPF, a VLA framework that performs unified spatiotemporal modeling in a compact physical token space. Spatially, WWH (What-Where-How) distills pretrained perception teachers exclusively during training into compact token groups capturing what 3D structures occupy the scene, where to interact, and how the gripper should approach, without test-time 3D encoders. Temporally, operating directly in this WWH space without pixel reconstruction, PPF (Past-Present-Future) consolidates executed states into a bounded past physical memory and jointly infers present and future physical tokens via an asymmetric world model. Parallel gated branches then inject these past, present, and future representations into a flow-matching action expert to guide manipulation without cross-temporal interference. Extensive experiments on SimplerEnv, CALVIN, and LIBERO show that PhysPPF consistently outperforms existing spatial, history-aware, and world-model VLAs with modest latency and parameter overhead, improving over the StarVLA baseline by +17.2 points on SimplerEnv, +29.3 points on CALVIN, and +3.5 points on LIBERO.
papers.title_zh: PhysPPF：用过去、现在、未来的物理表征学习机器人操作
papers.summary_zh: 在 VLA 中统一建模含三维接触线索的时空表征，兼顾精确接触和长程协调。

papers.title: SBTenv: A Literature-Validated Split-Belt Treadmill Simulation Environment
papers.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Code available at https://github.com/PhilipByrn3/sbtenv
papers.abstract: The split-belt treadmill is an important tool for studying human locomotor adaptation. Physics-based simulations complement such experiments by allowing hypotheses about the mechanisms of adaptation to be tested directly, and high-throughput simulation is increasingly needed as these models grow in complexity. However, no open-source split-belt treadmill environment exists in MuJoCo, a physics engine widely used for high-throughput simulation. Here, we present SBTenv, a split-belt treadmill environment built in MuJoCo and validated against published experimental data from a rimless wheel walking passively on a split-belt treadmill. By modeling compliant contacts at the spoke tips, SBTenv reproduces the experimental average steady velocity ($R^2=0.643$, RMSE $=0.0162$ m/s) without the empirical geometric correction required in prior simulations. We expect SBTenv, openly shared, to enable high-throughput simulation of musculoskeletal and robotic locomotion on a split-belt treadmill.

papers.title: Environment-Aware Probabilistic State Estimation of Continuum Robots from Planar Imaging
papers.abstract: Continuum robots are compliant along their entire length, making them well suited to navigating confined environments where contact with surrounding structures is often unavoidable. However, this compliance makes their modeling more complex compared to rigid robots, especially under contact, so their state must often be estimated from information available during operation. In many applications, the environment is known in advance, for example from preoperative imaging in medicine or from design models in industrial inspection. We present a probabilistic state estimator that represents the known environment as a signed distance field, informing the estimated shape. Continuous in arclength and time, it estimates the full state from asynchronous measurements anywhere along the robot. It also fuses planar images of body-fixed markers from a moving camera with commanded actuation, so the robot needs no embedded sensors. In a simulated aortic arch and a hardware phantom, the estimator tracked the robot into the target branch, and with a single view, using the known environment lowered the tip error from 2.5% to 1.6% and from 20.0% to 11.3% of the robot length, respectively. The continuous estimate of the full state and its uncertainty can support navigation and control of sensorless continuum robots.

papers.title: Lifted Multiple Shooting for Parallel-in-Time Contact-Rich Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: Planning through contact requires accounting for the coupled dynamics of a robot and its environment, including inertial effects, contact forces, and friction. However, the non-smoothness and multimodality of contact dynamics and contact geometry makes gradient-based optimization challenging. In this work, we propose lifted multiple shooting, a trajectory optimization transcription that can be solved directly using nonlinear program solvers. By introducing contact impulses as optimization variables, our formulation allows the optimizer to satisfy the state-transition constraints using friction-cone-feasible impulses while separately enforcing their consistency with the contact model. Our formulation supports a broad class of contact constitutive relations, with sensitivities computed through implicit differentiation. To enable efficient planning over long horizons and for high-dimensional systems, we further introduce IP-PAS, a parallel-in-time primal-dual interior-point solver that achieves O(log T) parallel computational depth. We evaluate the proposed methods on six fully dynamic contact-rich planning tasks, including nonprehensile pushing and in-hand manipulation, without contact-guiding costs. Lifted multiple shooting improves success rates by up to 81.5 percentage points over standard multiple shooting, while IP-PAS achieves solution quality comparable to serial methods with up to a 3.1x speedup and scales to horizons of 40,000 timesteps.

papers.title: Real-time Priority-aware UAS Arrival Planning Framework for Multi-layer UTM
papers.comment: Submitted to AIAA Journal of Aerospace and Information Systems
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a real-time, priority-aware UAS arrival-planning framework for multi-layer UTM terminal airspace represented as a funnel of concentric rings, discrete holding slots, connecting edges, and a landing pad. Managing dense arrivals is challenging because terminal resources are limited and UAS must remain spatially and temporally separated throughout their approaches. New arrivals, wind disturbances, and emergency landing requests further require rapid replanning beyond conventional landing-pad sequencing. To achieve computational tractability, the framework employs a greedy planning method that first establishes a priority-aware landing order and then plans the UAS sequentially. For each UAS, the method determines its slot assignments, traversal path, landing time, and slot entry and exit times while treating previously planned trajectories as fixed. Spatial and temporal constraints prevent conflicts on holding slots, connecting edges, and the landing pad. Within a rolling-horizon implementation, the framework incorporates new arrivals, reactively adjusts plans affected by wind disturbances, and prioritizes emergency UAS without altering completed operations. Computational results show that the method generates and updates feasible, conflict-free arrival plans within operational time limits while providing expedited landing access to emergency UAS. The results demonstrate the suitability of the proposed framework for responsive and safety-critical arrival management in dynamic multi-layer UTM environments. Video link: https://youtu.be/F9IP1dz-9PE
